newsitem.title: UNITED ARAB EMIRATES: Arafat meets UAE president, to go to Cairo.
newsitem.headline: Arafat meets UAE president, to go to Cairo.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat discussed Middle East peace prospects with the president of the United Arab Emirates on Saturday and then left for Qatar ahead of a scheduled visit to Cairo, officials said.
Passing through Jordan earlier on Saturday, Arafat said no real progress had been made in talks with Israel on the delayed handover to Palestinian self-rule of the West Bank town of Hebron.

UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan underlined the importance of abiding by peace agreements reached between Israel and Arab states. He stressed "the dangers of Israel going back on its pledges, a matter that could destroy efforts to implement peace and stability in the region", the official UAE news agency WAM reported.
A Palestinian official in Cairo said Arafat would visit the Egyptian capital on Sunday for talks with President Hosni Mubarak on the stalled Middle East peace process.

Zuhdi al-Qidra, the Palestinian Authority's ambassador to Cairo, said in a statement that Arafat would brief Mubarak on the failure of Palestinian-Israeli negotiations to reach agreement on Israel's pullout from Hebron.
Israel was to have withdrawn its troops from most of Hebron earlier this year but froze the pullout in response to a wave of Islamic suicide bombings in the Jewish state.
The withdrawal has been further delayed by peace talks deadlocked over Israel's demand that its forces be allowed to pursue suspected guerrillas into self-ruled areas.
Hebron, a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence, is the only West Bank town with a Jewish population. Some 400 Jews live in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs.

A spokesman at Qidra's office said it was not clear if Arafat would attend an Arab League emergency meeting to be held in Cairo on Sunday to discuss Israel's expansion of Jewish settlements on occupied Arab land.
Arafat left the United Arab Emirates for Doha, capital of Qatar. Earlier on Saturday he crossed into Jordan from Palestinian-ruled Jericho.
He was met at the Allenby Bridge by Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti and briefed him on the Palestinians' stalled talks with Israel over Hebron.

"No practical and tangible progress is being made on the ground because of the rejection by the Israeli side to implement what has been agreed," Arafat said, quoted by the Jordanian state news agency Petra.
Arafat said the Israeli negotiating team in talks on the redeployment of Israeli troops "wanted to change a number of key articles in the Hebron accord, which is what the Palestinian side rejects."
